_convention: One sentinel per page, unchanged. A page carries exactly one sentinel comment: the pass that last authored the file. That is what a sentinel has always meant here, and no page grows a second one.
_why: Which passes *authorise* the copy on a page is a different question from which pass last touched it, and it cannot be derived from the page. The closeout pass stamped its own sentinel over the accounts sentinel on privacy/index.html while leaving the accounts copy in place, and a verifier asking 'does this page carry the accounts sentinel' then reported a finding about neither the page nor the pass. So the relation is declared here, where it can be reviewed - the same class as gameIdOverrides, canonicalAliases, reclassifyAsGame and chooserLinkText.
_boundary: Copy is authorised by the pass whose feature's BEHAVIOUR it describes - not by every pass whose systems it names. The privacy page's accounts and mailing copy describes how the accounts feature behaves, so the accounts pass authorises it. The chooser's locked sentence names Supabase and Buttondown only as things the audience preference does NOT touch: it describes the audience-preference feature's behaviour, so the audience pass authorises it and the accounts pass does not. Name-matching would flag half the estate; this test does not.

members/index.html.note: Account-backed member data and its narrow scope. One pass, one sentinel, no ambiguity.

privacy/index.html.note: Three passes genuinely authorise copy here. The accounts pass authored the Supabase, Buttondown and deletion sections; the closeout pass authored the audience-choice, recent-items and same-origin-search sections; the maker-splash pass authored the mbm_splash_last disclosure. The page carries the maker-splash sentinel because that pass wrote it last. BACKLOG 0a-B.

stats/index.html.note: Device-local activity copy. Additionally asserted verbatim by the counter checks in verify_professional_site.js.

teach/index.html.note: Generated by tools/render_discovery_hubs.py; that renderer is its only writer. The closeout pass composed the page. The task-strip sentence describes what choosing a task DOES, and what it does was built by the teach-task-filter pass, so that pass authorises that sentence. The page carries the closeout sentinel because the renderer stamps it - one sentinel per page, as above. The footer support-pill sentence describes what supporting the work pays for, and that pill was built by the support-buttons pass, so that pass authorises it.

education-hub/index.html.note: Same renderer, same convention. Declared alongside its sibling because the teach-task-filter pass audited it for the same defect and changed the shared search behaviour it depends on, even though its own copy did not change. The support-buttons pass authorises the same footer support-pill sentence here, from the same shared record in data/support-pill.json.

resources/index.html.note: Ruled by Matt 2026-08-13: /resources/ is pupil-reachable (the pupil homepage's no-JS search fallback posts to it), so the Ko-fi pill it carried from before the support-buttons pass is REMOVED rather than ratified. The removal deletes authored copy - the pill's free-to-use sentence - so this pass authorises that page's copy change and stamps its sentinel. The page had no sentinel before; one page, one sentinel, as above.

games/index.html.note: Ruled by Matt 2026-08-14, extending the 2026-08-13 ruling that closed /resources/: no commerce on pupil-reachable surfaces. The arcade is the page the pupil homepage links straight to, and it carried a page-local <a class="kofi"> anchor of its own - outside data/support-pill.json entirely, so neither that record nor check_support_pill() had ever seen it. Removing it deletes authored copy (the 'Buy me a coffee' label), which is why the page is declared here. Two passes genuinely authorise copy on it, as on privacy/index.html: games-audience-faces authored the arcade and owns the sentinel the page must keep - verify_games_audience_faces.py pins it as GAMES_SENTINEL and the browser suite re-checks it, so it cannot be restamped the way /resources/ was - and support-buttons owns the commerce copy being removed. Declaring the page moves it from byte-exact authored-copy comparison to sentinel authorisation. That is a real relaxation and is stated rather than glossed; against it, the specific thing that changed is now pinned harder than before in the opposite direction, because games/index.html joined PILL_FORBIDDEN with its own positive control where previously nothing pinned it at all. The logo-visual check on this page is unaffected: it runs before the branch.

main/index.html.note: Recorded on purpose rather than left to escape by accident. This page carries accounts/mailing prose and device-local-counter prose and no sentinel at all, because it is governed by the HOME_TRUTH_REGIONS comparison instead - each authorised region is replaced by a placeholder before the preservation diff, so the copy is pinned more tightly than a sentinel would pin it. Declaring that here is the decision, not the absence of one.

tools/index.html._why: The accreditation-card inventory region remains the only free-copy region. Matt additionally approved the education tools refresh on 2026-09-05: exact hero and shortcut copy, the browse/footer domain wording and moving the existing tools drawer before the feature panels. educationRefresh records both sides of each accepted copy change and the two allowed section orders. Every other word, including the accreditation bridge and utility cards, remains preservation-protected; this page stays governed by region-comparison and gains no sentinel exemption.

educationRefresh.note: D4 landing note §6: the old Find & browse cards (Resource Search, Creator Hub) are the Resources and Tools pages themselves and were removed by design, so resource-search-description is retired from exactReplacements.
